title: TSM Construction Recovery: Plan And Decide
story: PROJECT AT RISK > RECOVERY PLAN > DECISIONS AND AUDIT
desc: A seeded demo project (Ameris medical office building, phase two) run through the real recovery routes: ranked exposures, a recovery plan, gated change-order decisions and a durable audit trail. Sample data, not a live client system.
_note: Captured against the real Construction recovery routes with seeded sample data (lib/construction-recovery.js). No mocked engine output. Drafts use the template fallback unless the capture is run with KEEP_GROQ=1. The audit trail is written to a throwaway directory that the wrapper deletes.

states.caption: The construction war room, with a new Recovery tab
states.narration: This is the construction war room. A new recovery tab tracks a seeded demo project, a forty-eight million dollar medical office building. Everything you see runs on sample data, not a live client system.

states.caption: Recovery tab - 9 weeks behind, $3.1M over forecast
states.narration: The recovery tab opens inside the war room. At the top, the project is nine weeks behind schedule, with a forecast overrun of three point one million dollars.

states.caption: The same view, full size
states.narration: Here is the same view at full size. Nine weeks behind, a forecast overrun of three point one million dollars, and forty-one open exposures across requests for information, change orders and late submittals.

states.caption: Recovery plan - four actions, five weeks back
states.narration: The recovery plan has four actions: a second electrical crew, fast-tracked answers on the critical-path requests, approval of the critical-path change orders, and overlapping the envelope and interior work. Together they pull back five weeks and bring the forecast overrun down to one point four million dollars.

states.caption: 41 exposures, ranked by dollars, delay and critical path
states.narration: Every open exposure is ranked by the dollars at risk, the schedule impact, and whether it sits on the critical path. The electrical gear resequencing change order is at the top.

states.caption: 11 pending change orders, $2.7M in total
states.narration: On the right are the eleven pending change orders, worth two point seven million dollars in total. Each one carries a recommendation and the reason behind it.

states.caption: A draft is prepared for review - nothing is sent
states.narration: For any change order, a draft can be prepared from the project record. It is a draft for a person to review. Nothing is sent and nothing is approved by this step.

states.caption: Accepting takes two clicks
states.narration: To accept a recommendation, the first click only arms the button.

states.caption: Decision recorded - the audit entry is written first
states.narration: The second click records the decision. The audit entry is written first, and if the audit trail were unavailable, the decision would be refused.

states.caption: An override without a real reason is blocked
states.narration: A person can disagree with a recommendation, but an override needs a written reason. Here the reason is too short, so the system blocks it.

states.caption: Override recorded, with its reason
states.narration: With a real reason in writing, the override goes through. The card shows that it was an override, and why.

states.caption: Every decision is in the audit trail
states.narration: Every decision lands in the audit trail, with the change order, who made it, and when. The system ranks and recommends, a person decides, and the record is kept.
